title: Sticky Toffee Pudding
description: A dark, moist date sponge soaked in a salted toffee sauce, served warm with cold cream or vanilla ice cream.
intro: There are few better ends to a Sunday dinner. The dates melt into the sponge, keeping it impossibly moist, and the sauce is poured over twice: once to soak in, once to serve.
It reheats beautifully, so it's an ideal make-ahead pudding for a crowd.

items.note: soft, plus extra for the tin

method.title: Soak the dates
method.text: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and butter a 20 × 20cm baking dish. Pour the boiling water over the dates, stir in the bicarbonate of soda and leave for 10 minutes. Mash roughly with a fork.

method.title: Make the batter
method.text: Beat the butter and sugar until light, then beat in the eggs one at a time. Fold in the flour, then the dates and their liquid and the vanilla. It will be a loose batter.

method.title: Bake
method.text: Pour into the dish and bake for 30–35 minutes until risen and a skewer comes out clean.

method.title: Make the sauce
method.text: Meanwhile, melt the butter and sugar in a pan, stirring, then add the cream and salt. Bring to the boil and bubble for 3–4 minutes until glossy and slightly thickened.

method.title: Soak and serve
method.text: Prick the warm sponge all over with a skewer and pour over a third of the sauce. Leave for 10 minutes to soak in. Cut into squares and serve with the remaining warm sauce and cream or ice cream.

tips: Medjool dates are softer and more caramel-like than standard dried dates and make a noticeably richer sponge.
Make the sponge up to 2 days ahead. Reheat, covered, at 160°C for 15 minutes, then pour over the sauce.

substitutions.note: Dark soft brown sugar plus 1 tbsp black treacle.
Use plain flour with 2 tsp baking powder.
